vulnerability_type: Denial of Service via Uncontrolled Recursion (Stack Exhaustion)
llm_poc_idea: In catalog.c::xmlParseSGMLCatalog(), when depth approaches MAX_CATAL_DEPTH=50, feed SGML Catalog with multiple self-referencing CATALOG directives (e.g., CATALOG "./self.cat" where sysid resolves back to same file) to trigger Denial of Service via Uncontrolled Recursion (stack exhaustion).
_cot_summary: The diff modifies xmlParseSGMLCatalog() in catalog.c to add deduplication before calling xmlExpandCatalog(). Previously, the resolved filename was passed directly to xmlExpandCatalog() without checking for duplicates. The patch introduces a new xmlCatalogEntryPtr entry created via xmlNewCatalogEntry(), registers it in catal->sgml via xmlHashAddEntry(), and only calls xmlExpandCatalog() if the hash insertion succeeds (res >= 0), otherwise calling xmlFreeCatalogEntry() to prevent duplicate recursive expansion.
_poc_malicious_input: SGML catalog file containing multiple CATALOG directives where sysid resolves to the catalog file itself (e.g., CATALOG "./evil.cat" repeated K times inside evil.cat)
_poc_impact: Stack overflow crash due to K^50 uncontrolled recursive invocations of xmlExpandCatalog/xmlParseSGMLCatalog

llm_poc_idea: In uri.c::xmlBuildRelativeURISafe(), when ix=INT_MAX+1 (wrapping to negative on int), feed XML parser with URI and base containing a path exceeding 2.14 GB to trigger out-of-bounds read via signed integer overflow on ix and heap buffer overflow via 3 * nbslash wrapping in xmlMalloc.
_cot_summary: The diff changes variables ix, nbslash, len, and pos from int to size_t in xmlBuildRelativeURISafe. It also adds an overflow guard checking len + 3 * nbslash > SIZE_MAX before the xmlMalloc allocation, and casts the xmlStrlen(uptr) result to size_t before assigning to len.
_poc_malicious_input: URI and base parameters with path components totaling > INT_MAX bytes (~2.14 GB), causing ix to overflow to negative values during the path comparison loop
_poc_impact: Out-of-bounds read during path traversal via overflowed ix index, and heap buffer overflow via undersized xmlMalloc allocation when 3 * nbslash wraps

llm_poc_idea: In relaxng.c::xmlRelaxNGValidateValue(), when ctxt->state->value != ctxt->state->endvalue, feed RelaxNG validator with crafted XML containing list values with trailing extra tokens to trigger XML_RELAXNG_ERR_LISTEXTRA error path storing raw pointer via VALID_ERR2, then free ctxt->state->value to trigger Use-After-Free.
_cot_summary: In relaxng.c::xmlRelaxNGValidateValue(), the macro call VALID_ERR2 is replaced with VALID_ERR2P when reporting error XML_RELAXNG_ERR_LISTEXTRA with argument ctxt->state->value. The 'P' variant (duplicating variant) copies the string rather than storing a direct pointer to ctxt->state->value.
_poc_malicious_input: XML document with list-typed data containing extra unconsumed values so ctxt->state->value != ctxt->state->endvalue triggers XML_RELAXNG_ERR_LISTEXTRA
_poc_impact: Use-after-free leading to heap memory access after free, potential code execution or denial of service crash

vulnerability_type: Denial of Service via Uncontrolled Recursion (Stack Exhaustion)
llm_poc_idea: In relaxng.c::xmlRelaxNGLoadInclude(), when incNr grows unbounded via recursive include processing, feed RelaxNG parser with crafted schema containing deeply chained include elements referencing successive schemas to trigger stack exhaustion / memory exhaustion.
_cot_summary: The diff adds an inclusion depth limit to the RelaxNG parser. It introduces _xmlRelaxNGIncludeLimit (default 1000), a new field incLimit in _xmlRelaxNGParserCtxt, and function xmlRelaxParserSetIncLImit. The function xmlRelaxNGIncludePush now checks ctxt->incNr >= ctxt->incLimit and returns -1 on overflow. The xmlRelaxNGParse function reads the RNG_INCLUDE_LIMIT environment variable to override the default.
_poc_malicious_input: RelaxNG schema file with deeply nested <include href='...'> directives creating a chain of 1000+ inclusions
_poc_impact: Stack exhaustion or memory exhaustion causing process crash (Denial of Service)

llm_poc_idea: In xmlwriter.c::xmlTextWriterStartElementNS(), when writer->nsstack=NULL due to a prior error path, feed XML Writer with a crafted sequence of namespace operations that corrupts the writer state to trigger NULL pointer dereference in xmlListEmpty(writer->nsstack) causing Denial of Service.
_cot_summary: The diff adds NULL pointer validation for writer->nsstack in three functions: xmlTextWriterStartElementNS, xmlTextWriterStartAttributeNS, and xmlTextWriterOutputNSDecl. Without these checks, if writer->nsstack is NULL, subsequent calls to xmlListEmpty(writer->nsstack) would dereference a NULL pointer, causing a crash.
_poc_malicious_input: writer->nsstack = NULL (corrupt writer state), with any non-NULL, non-empty name parameter
_poc_impact: NULL pointer dereference crash in xmlListEmpty(writer->nsstack), causing Denial of Service

llm_poc_idea: In docker/docker_client.go::getOCIDescriptorContents(), when desc.Digest contains a malformed value, feed a malicious registry response with a manifest containing an invalid digest string in desc.Digest to trigger panic in desc.Digest.Algorithm().
_cot_summary: The function getOCIDescriptorContents in docker/docker_client.go adds three security checks: (1) desc.Digest.Validate() to prevent a potential panic when desc.Digest.Algorithm() is called, (2) digestAlgorithm.Available() to reject unsupported algorithms, and (3) after reading payload, computes actualDigest via digestAlgorithm.FromBytes(payload) and compares it against desc.Digest to verify the downloaded blob's integrity.
_poc_malicious_input: desc.Digest field set to an invalid/malformed digest string (e.g., empty or syntactically broken)
_poc_impact: Go runtime panic causing process termination and denial of service

llm_poc_idea: In server.go::Close(), when s.listeners is being iterated without s.locker held, feed the SMTP server with rapid concurrent connections while the server operator invokes Close(), triggering a data-race panic on s.listeners to trigger Denial of Service via Panic.
_cot_summary: The diff moves s.locker.Lock() from after the s.listeners loop to before it in the Close() method. In the original code, the for _, l := range s.listeners loop executed without holding s.locker, meaning concurrent modifications to s.listeners caused a data race. The fix ensures both s.listeners and s.conns are iterated under the same lock.
_poc_malicious_input: Rapidly open and close SMTP connections to populate s.conns while Close() is invoked by the server, racing the unlocked s.listeners iteration.
_poc_impact: Go runtime panic due to data race on s.listeners slice, causing SMTP server process crash and denial of service.

llm_poc_idea: In src/rdpng.c::start_input_png(), when maxval=65535 and cinfo->data_precision=16, feed PNG decoder with crafted 16-bit-per-component PNG triggering signed overflow in val * ((1 << cinfo->data_precision) - 1) + half_maxval on ILP32 to trigger undefined behavior in rescale array computation.
_cot_summary: In start_input_png() in src/rdpng.c, the types of variables val and half_maxval are changed from long to size_t. The allocation and memset calls for source->rescale are simplified by removing explicit casts, and the loop condition changes from val <= (long)maxval to val <= maxval. This prevents signed integer overflow in the rescale computation on ILP32 systems.
_poc_impact: Signed integer overflow (undefined behavior) in rescale computation leading to incorrect sample values or potential memory safety issues from UB

llm_poc_idea: In turbojpeg.c::getSubsamp(), when a JPEG with 4:1:0 subsampling factors is parsed via tj3DecompressHeader(), feed crafted JPEG with component sampling factors matching TJSAMP_410 pattern to trigger subsamp=7, causing out-of-bounds read on caller's static tjMCUWidth[7] and tjMCUHeight[7] arrays sized for only 7 elements.
_cot_summary: The diff introduces API versioning by renaming tj3Init() to tj3InitVersion() with an apiVersion parameter, redefining tj3Init() as a macro in turbojpeg.h that passes TURBOJPEG_VERSION_NUMBER. A new numSamp field in tjinstance is set to TJ_NUMSAMP for apiVersion >= 3002000, or 7 for older callers, and all subsamp bounds checks are changed from TJ_NUMSAMP to this->numSamp. The function getSubsamp() now iterates up to this->numSamp instead of TJ_NUMSAMP, preventing newer subsampling constants from being exposed to older callers.
_poc_malicious_input: A JPEG file with component sampling factors matching the TJSAMP_410 or TJSAMP_24 patterns recognized in getSubsamp() (e.g., 4:1:0 subsampling with h_sampling=[4,1,1], v_sampling=[1,1,1] or 2:4 subsampling patterns)
_poc_impact: Out-of-bounds read on caller's static tjMCUWidth[] and tjMCUHeight[] arrays, potentially causing crash or information disclosure

llm_poc_idea: In turbojpeg-jni.c::TJCompressor_loadSourceImage(), when width=32768 and height=16384 and pixelFormat=4, feed TJCompressor with crafted image dimensions triggering width*height*tjPixelSize=2147483648 (between INT_MAX and UINT_MAX) to trigger signed integer overflow in arraySize and subsequent Heap Buffer Overflow.
_cot_summary: The diff replaces overflow thresholds from (unsigned int)-1 (UINT_MAX) to INT_MAX in six JNI functions in turbojpeg-jni.c: TJCompressor_compress, TJCompressor_encodeYUV8, TJDecompressor_decompress, TJDecompressor_decodeYUV8, TJCompressor_loadSourceImage, and TJDecompressor_saveImage. Additionally, TJCompressor_loadSourceImage changes its size calculation from width*height*tjPixelSize to PAD(width*tjPixelSize, align)*height to account for row padding, and TJDecompressor_saveImage restructures its check to use actualPitch*height instead of width*height*tjPixelSize.
_poc_malicious_input: width=32768, height=16384, pixelFormat=4 (TJPF_RGBX) yields width*height*tjPixelSize=2147483648 (INT_MAX+1), passing UINT_MAX check but overflowing signed int to -2147483648
_poc_impact: Heap buffer overwrite in native C code via JNI, potential code execution in the JVM process

llm_poc_idea: In src/rdpng.c::finish_input_png(), when source->ctx points to already-freed memory due to a prior error-path cleanup, feed PNG decoder with a malformed PNG triggering a secondary error path that re-invokes finish_input_png() to trigger Double Free of source->ctx.
_cot_summary: The diff adds source->ctx = NULL after spng_ctx_free(source->ctx) in finish_input_png (src/rdpng.c) and dest->ctx = NULL after spng_ctx_free(dest->ctx) in finish_output_png (src/wrpng.c). These null assignments prevent the pointers from being freed again if the respective finish methods are called multiple times.
_poc_malicious_input: A crafted PNG file that causes an error condition during decoding/compression which triggers cleanup (finish_input_png or finish_output_png) to be called twice on the same source/dest object
_poc_impact: Double free of the spng context on the heap, leading to heap metadata corruption and potential arbitrary code execution

vulnerability_type: Denial of Service via Infinite Loop
llm_poc_idea: In src/spng/miniz.c::tinfl_decompress(), when code_len=0 after Huffman table lookup, feed PNG/deflate parser with crafted compressed stream containing degenerate Huffman codes to trigger Denial of Service via Infinite Loop.
_cot_summary: The diff adds two guards in tinfl_decompress() within src/spng/miniz.c. After executing bit_buf >>= code_len and num_bits -= code_len, each guard checks if code_len == 0 and, if true, returns TINFL_STATUS_FAILED via TINFL_CR_RETURN_FOREVER at coroutine states 40 and 54 respectively.
_poc_malicious_input: Crafted deflate-compressed data stream containing Huffman-coded symbols that produce code_len=0 during decompression lookup
_poc_impact: Infinite loop causing CPU exhaustion and timeout; application hangs indefinitely processing the malformed compressed payload

vulnerability_type: Denial of Service via Infinite Loop
llm_poc_idea: In parser.rs::spans(), when text="\x1b[2J", feed the parser with ANSI input containing unsupported escape sequence text="\x1b[2J" to trigger infinite loop because style() cannot consume the sequence and text is never advanced.
_cot_summary: The diff restructures the ANSI parser in parser.rs. The original style() used tag("\x1b[") + separated_list0 of ansi_item + alt(char('m'),char('h'),char('l')), which failed on unsupported escape sequences without consuming input. The new code adds ansi_sgr_code() for SGR parsing and any_escape_sequence() using preceded/delimited/take_till to consume any unrecognized escape sequence. The spans() loop is changed from unconditional loop with ? to while let Ok(...).
_poc_malicious_input: text field containing bytes \x1b[2J (CSI clear screen) or \x1b[?25l (cursor hide) — any CSI sequence not terminating in m/h/l
_poc_impact: Application hang / infinite loop consuming CPU, denial of service

llm_poc_idea: In archive_read_support_format_cab.c::cab_read_ahead_cfdata_lzx(), when cfdata->uncompressed_size > cab->uncompressed_buffer_size, feed CAB parser with crafted CFDATA block having uncompressed_size set to an oversized value to trigger Heap Out-of-Bounds Write during LZX decompression into cab->uncompressed_buffer.
_cot_summary: The diff adds a bounds check in cab_read_ahead_cfdata_lzx() in archive_read_support_format_cab.c. Before decompression proceeds, it now validates that cfdata->uncompressed_size does not exceed cab->uncompressed_buffer_size. If the check fails, it sets *avail to ARCHIVE_FATAL and returns NULL with an error message.
_poc_malicious_input: cfdata->uncompressed_size field in a CAB CFDATA block set to a value larger than cab->uncompressed_buffer_size
_poc_impact: Heap buffer overflow during LZX decompression, potential arbitrary code execution or crash

llm_poc_idea: In archive_read_support_format_cab.c::cab_checksum_finish(), when cfdata->memimage=NULL, feed CAB parser with crafted CAB file triggering skip path with RESERVE_PRESENT flag set to trigger null pointer dereference crash.
_cot_summary: The diff adds a NULL pointer guard in cab_checksum_finish() in archive_read_support_format_cab.c. After computing l based on cab->cfheader.flags and cab->cfheader.cfdata, the new code checks if cfdata->memimage is NULL and returns ARCHIVE_FAILED before dereferencing it at cfdata->memimage + CFDATA_cbData.
_poc_malicious_input: CAB file with RESERVE_PRESENT flag set in cfheader.flags where a skip operation causes cfdata->memimage to remain NULL
_poc_impact: Null pointer dereference causing SIGSEGV crash in the library process

llm_poc_idea: In contrib/untar.c::parseoct(), when n=0 and *p is at buffer boundary, feed tar archive with crafted header field where all bytes are non-octal (e.g., all spaces) so the first while loop decrements n to 0 and then dereferences *p past buffer end to trigger Out-of-Bounds Read.
_cot_summary: The diff modifies the parseoct function in contrib/untar.c by moving the n > 0 check before the *p dereference in both while loops. This ensures that when n equals 0 the pointer p is never dereferenced, preventing a one-byte out-of-bounds read past the buffer.
_poc_malicious_input: A tar header octal field (e.g., size or mode field) positioned such that all n bytes are consumed by leading non-octal characters or the field ends with n=0 while p is at buffer end
_poc_impact: One-byte out-of-bounds read past the valid buffer boundary, potentially leaking adjacent memory or causing a crash

llm_poc_idea: In libarchive_linkify_fuzzer.cc::LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(), when archive_entry_linkify(resolver, &entry, &spare) caches entry (entry=NULL) for a hardlink pair, feed fuzzer input with two entries sharing the same nlink values to trigger double-free of the same archive_entry object via the resolver drain loop and the final entries[i] cleanup loop.
_cot_summary: The diff modifies LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput in libarchive_linkify_fuzzer.cc. After archive_entry_linkify(resolver, &entry, &spare) is called, the patch adds entries[i] = entry; to update the tracking array when linkify takes ownership of or swaps the entry. The final cleanup loop now correctly only frees entries not consumed by the resolver.
_poc_malicious_input: buf containing crafted archive entries with matching hardlink nlink values that cause archive_entry_linkify to cache entry (setting entry=NULL) or return a swapped entry via spare
_poc_impact: double-free crash in fuzzer process — archive_entry_free called twice on the same heap object

llm_poc_idea: In lib/nghttp2_submit.c::nghttp2_submit_origin(), when a custom allocator is configured via mem and a subsequent allocation fails reaching fail_item_malloc, feed the session with parameters triggering ov_copy allocation followed by failure to trigger mismatched free() on custom-allocated memory.
_cot_summary: The diff changes a single line in nghttp2_submit_origin() in lib/nghttp2_submit.c. At the fail_item_malloc error label, free(ov_copy) is replaced with nghttp2_mem_free(mem, ov_copy) so that the deallocator matches the nghttp2_mem_malloc() allocator used to create ov_copy.
_poc_malicious_input: Application configures custom nghttp2_mem allocator, then calls nghttp2_submit_origin under memory pressure causing the internal allocation after ov_copy to fail, reaching fail_item_malloc.
_poc_impact: Heap metadata corruption via mismatched deallocator (free() on custom-allocated memory), potentially leading to denial of service or exploitable memory corruption.
